title: New load-balancing strategies and RoundRobin deprecation

detection.reason: the load-balancing strategy is set per service under spec.routes[].services[], nested inside the routes array rather than at the top level of the projection

quote: Starting with v3.4, HTTP service definitions now support additional load-balancing strategies for better traffic distribution.
remediation: Apply the updated CRDs, then move any service using `RoundRobin` to `wrr` — the two are equivalent and `RoundRobin` is removed in the next major release. `p2c` (Power of Two Choices) is the new option worth considering for uneven backend load.
verifyCommand: kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $o | .spec.routes[]?.services[]? | select(.strategy == "RoundRobin") | $o.metadata.namespace + "/" + $o.metadata.name' # names printed use the deprecated strategy value

title: MultiPath TCP support removed again

detection.reason: this is Traefik static or provider configuration, not a field on any collected Kubernetes object

quote: Since `v3.4.5`, the MultiPath TCP support introduced with `v3.4.2` has been removed.
remediation: Only relevant if MPTCP was enabled during the 3.4.2–3.4.4 window; remove that configuration. It was withdrawn because enabling it on some platforms could stop Traefik outright.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy,ds -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.template.spec.containers[]; .image | test("(^|/)(mirrored-library-|library-)?traefik([:@]|$)"))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) replicas=\(.spec.replicas // "per-node")", (.spec.template.spec.containers[] | (.args // [])[]), (.spec.template.spec.containers[] | (.env // [])[] | "env \(.name)")' | grep -iE '^(Deployment|DaemonSet) |multipath|mptcp' # nothing printed means MPTCP was never enabled and the removal is a no-op; a static configuration file mounted from a ConfigMap is not listed, read it too

title: Request paths normalized per RFC 3986

detection.reason: this is request-time behaviour, not a property of any collected object

quote: Starting with v3.4.1, request paths are now normalized according to RFC 3986 standards for better consistency and security.
remediation: Read with the reserved-character change landing in the same release: unreserved characters are decoded and percent-encodings uppercased. Rules matching on a specific encoding of the path need re-testing against real request URLs.
verifyCommand: ( kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $r | .spec.routes[]? | "\($r.metadata.namespace)/\($r.metadata.name)  \(.match)"'; kubectl get ingress -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $i | .spec.rules[]?.http.paths[]? | "\($i.metadata.namespace)/\($i.metadata.name)  \(.path // "")"' ) | grep -E '%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}' # rules printed match on a percent-encoded path; re-test them against real request URLs, unreserved characters are decoded and encodings uppercased

title: Reserved characters stay encoded during router rule matching

detection.reason: the router rule lives in spec.routes[].match, nested inside the routes array; the evaluator matches only TOP-LEVEL fields of the collected projection

quote: Starting with v3.4.1, reserved characters (per RFC 3986) remain encoded during router rule matching to prevent routing ambiguity.
remediation: The upstream note's own table is the thing to check: a path like `/foo%2Fbar` no longer matches a rule written as if the encoded slash were decoded. Any rule that depended on an encoded separator being decoded before matching must be rewritten.
verifyCommand: ( kubectl get ingressroutes.traefik.io -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $r | .spec.routes[]? | "\($r.metadata.namespace)/\($r.metadata.name)  \(.match)"'; kubectl get ingress -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | . as $i | .spec.rules[]?.http.paths[]? | "\($i.metadata.namespace)/\($i.metadata.name)  \(.path // "")"' ) | grep -E '%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}' # rules printed match on a percent-encoded path; a rule that relied on an encoded separator being decoded before matching no longer matches

title: Rule syntax compatibility options are going away

detection.reason: checked in the Traefik workload's container args only (Deployment or DaemonSet) — an option set through a static configuration file or environment variables is not scanned

quote: In v3.4, rule syntax configuration options will be removed in the next major version.
remediation: `core.defaultRuleSyntax` and the per-router `ruleSyntax` option were transitional helpers for the v2-to-v3 migration and are removed in the next major version. Any router still relying on v2 rule syntax has to be migrated before then — this is the deadline for finishing the 3.0 router-rule work, not a new change in itself.
